host/native/build-dtn.lisp:354-365
        (defun fn-native-entry (st)
          (declare (ignore st))
          (fnn-crypto-startup)
          (fnn-tls-reset)
          (fnn-tls-initialize)

whereas host/native/build.lisp:481-490 wraps the same calls: (fnn-native-startup (lambda () (fnn-crypto-startup) ...)) and io.lisp:8636-8641 turns any serious-condition into 'fn-host: error: refused start: ...' with +fnn-exit-usage+ (5) after fnn-open-streams.
fix: Use the same (fnn-native-startup (lambda () ...)) wrapper build.lisp uses. Better, define the startup thunk once in io.lisp and have both build scripts call it, so the two entry points cannot drift.

reviewer: host/native/build-dtn.lisp:354-365 calls fnn-crypto-startup, the TLS, digest, hsig and deflate inits bare, without wrapping them in fnn-native-startup. host/native/build.lisp:481-490 does wrap them, and io.lisp:8636-8641 maps the error to 'refused start' with exit 5. The io.lisp comment at :8629-8635 records what happens unwrapped: the error reaches the --disable-debugger hook, ACL2's loop catches it, and the process prints a prompt and waits on stdin (native-subsets 47bdb9a4 failure 5). That is a hang, which is worse than the exit 1 the finding describes. The DTN image is a non-deployment fallback (build-dtn.lisp:8-13), which caps the severity.
scenario: A DTN image (fn-host-dtn, which build-dtn.lisp's header names a fallback and which cut gate 09 builds) is started on a host where the bundled libsodium, the system libssl 3 or libfn-blake3 does not load or fails its vector check. The error escapes fn-native-entry before fnn-open-streams. Under --disable-debugger SBCL prints a backtrace and exits 1, which outcome-class maps to :refused, a 'known refusal with a stable reason'. Alternatively ACL2's LP prints its own abort, depending on the handler in effect. A supervisor or test sees a refusal code with no 'refused start' line, rather than the usage/fault outcome the production image gives for the same failure.
title: DTN images run the native-library startup checks outside fnn-native-startup, so a failed check is not the documented refused start (exit 5)
